---
title: "Contrast environment screen"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
df-print: kable
---

Purpose: a first, cheap look at whether the subadult - adult contrast changes with weather
(option D, 2026-11-26; README "Downstream models"). It uses **no stage 1 output**: each
co-sampled survey event gives an empirical contrast with its sampling standard error, and a small
meta-regression across events and species asks whether those contrasts move with the weather at
the event. If it shows a signal, per-species moderation refits of stage 1 (option B) are the
formal follow-up.

What this can and cannot say:

- **seasonal-environmental, not weather**: raw 30-day temperature and 10-day precipitation are
  confounded with season (behavior, cohort growth, breeding). Only a climatology / anomaly split
  would support a weather interpretation.
- **co-sampled events only**: the only units that carry information about a stage x environment
  interaction. Species with few co-sampled events add little; *R. sierrae* has the most, but
  species-varying slopes keep it from setting the mean slope on its own.
- **between-site climate from long-term normals**: the site mean of swab-date weather is
  "climate at sampling time" (a summer-only site looks warm), so between-site terms use CHELSA
  bioclim 1981-2010 at site coordinates (`size_bd_unified/site_bioclim.Rmd`; added 2026-11-26):
  annual mean temperature, temperature seasonality, annual precipitation, precipitation
  seasonality, centered within species. Their slopes rest on species with co-sampled events at
  several sites in different climates (mostly the data-rich *Rana*).

Run order: `size_bd_unified/01_model_data.Rmd` (model data), `size_bd_unified/site_bioclim.Rmd`
(site climate), `01_contrast_tiers.Rmd` (species table), then this script. Fits are small (hundreds of rows) and cached with `file =`.

# Setup
```{r}
#| eval: true
#| output: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show setup code"

librarian::shelf(tidyverse, here, brms, cmdstanr, posterior, tidybayes)

screen_dir = here("size_bd_contrast", "models", "environment_screen")
dir.create(screen_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
intermediates_dir = here("size_bd_contrast", "intermediates")

# data file created by size_bd_unified/01_model_data.Rmd
load(here("size_bd_unified", "intermediates", "bd_model_env_unified_2026-11-12.RData"))

# constants (min_swabs_unit, response_col), add_contrast_groups()
source(here("size_bd_contrast", "contrast_data_functions.R"))
# conv_check() (shared with the seasonal and contrast models)
source(here("size_bd_season", "season_check_functions.R"))

set_cmdstan_path(Sys.getenv("cmd_stan_path"))

# long-term site climate (CHELSA bioclim 1981-2010; size_bd_unified/site_bioclim.Rmd)
site_bioclim = read_csv(here("size_bd_unified", "intermediates", "site_bioclim.csv"),
                        col_types = cols(site = "c", kg_code_3 = "c"))

# included species (01_contrast_tiers.Rmd)
species_table = read_csv(file.path(intermediates_dir, "01_contrast_species.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
included = species_table %>% filter(include) %>% pull(taxon_capture)

# load events need a spread of log load in each stage: >= 2 positives per stage (one more than
# the load co-sampling rule, which needs only >= 1)
min_pos_screen = 2

```

# Events and climate
```{r}
contrast_data = brms_data %>%
  filter(taxon_capture %in% included) %>%
  add_contrast_groups() %>%
  mutate(temp = temp_c_30_day_mean,
         # precipitation on log2(1 + mm): a slope per doubling of 10-day rainfall
         precip = log2(1 + precip_mm_10_day_sum),
         log_load = if_else(.data[[response_col]] > 0, log(.data[[response_col]]), NA_real_))

# one row per event (all events, single-stage ones included: they define the site-year and site
# reference conditions). climate = mean over the event's swabs (79% of events are one day)
events = contrast_data %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, population, year, pop_year, pop_year_event) %>%
  summarise(temp = mean(temp), precip = mean(precip),
            n_ad = sum(life_stage_simple == "adult"),
            n_sub = sum(life_stage_simple == "subadult"),
            pos_ad = sum(life_stage_simple == "adult" & !is.na(log_load)),
            pos_sub = sum(life_stage_simple == "subadult" & !is.na(log_load)),
            mean_ll_ad = mean(log_load[life_stage_simple == "adult"], na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_ll_sub = mean(log_load[life_stage_simple == "subadult"], na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

# swab-date weather split into two parts, within species:
#   *_within  event - its site-year mean      (within season)
#   *_year    site-year mean - its site mean  (between years at a site)
# means are over events, so each event counts once whatever its swab count. (the site mean of
# swab-date weather is not used between sites: it is climate at sampling time)
events = events %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, pop_year) %>%
  mutate(temp_py = mean(temp), precip_py = mean(precip)) %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, population) %>%
  mutate(temp_pop = mean(temp_py), precip_pop = mean(precip_py)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(temp_within = temp - temp_py, precip_within = precip - precip_py,
         temp_year = temp_py - temp_pop, precip_year = precip_py - precip_pop)

# between sites: long-term climate of each population (mean over its sites, each site weighted
# equally), centered within species on the mean over the species' populations. scaled so each
# slope reads per a meaningful step:
#   site_temp         annual mean temperature (bio1), per degree C
#   site_temp_seas    temperature seasonality (bio4 / 100 = sd of monthly means), per degree C of sd
#   site_precip       annual precipitation (log2 bio12), per doubling
#   site_precip_seas  precipitation seasonality (bio15 / 10), per 10 points of coefficient of variation
population_climate = contrast_data %>%
  distinct(taxon_capture, population, site = as.character(site)) %>%
  left_join(site_bioclim, by = "site") %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, population) %>%
  summarise(site_temp = mean(bio1_temp_mean),
            site_temp_seas = mean(bio4_temp_seasonality) / 100,
            site_precip = log2(mean(bio12_precip_annual)),
            site_precip_seas = mean(bio15_precip_seasonality) / 10,
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("site_"), ~ .x - mean(.x))) %>%
  ungroup()

# populations without site climate (expected: none)
population_climate %>% filter(if_any(starts_with("site_"), is.na))

events = events %>% left_join(population_climate, by = c("taxon_capture", "population"))

```

# Empirical contrasts
```{r}
# prevalence: empirical logit difference, subadult - adult (positive = subadults more often
# infected), with 0.5 added to each cell so 0/5 or 5/5 stay finite (Haldane correction).
# se = sqrt(sum of 1 / (cell + 0.5)) over the four cells
prev_events = events %>%
  filter(n_ad >= min_swabs_unit, n_sub >= min_swabs_unit) %>%
  mutate(contrast = log((pos_sub + 0.5) / (n_sub - pos_sub + 0.5)) -
           log((pos_ad + 0.5) / (n_ad - pos_ad + 0.5)),
         se = sqrt(1 / (pos_sub + 0.5) + 1 / (n_sub - pos_sub + 0.5) +
                     1 / (pos_ad + 0.5) + 1 / (n_ad - pos_ad + 0.5)))

# load: difference in mean log load among positives, subadult - adult. the se uses each species'
# pooled within-event sd of log load (2-3 positives alone give an unstable sd): residuals of log
# load around their event x stage mean, over all events with >= 2 positives in that stage
sd_log_load = contrast_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(log_load)) %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, pop_year_event, life_stage_simple) %>%
  filter(n() >= 2) %>%
  mutate(resid = log_load - mean(log_load)) %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture) %>%
  summarise(sd_ll = sqrt(sum(resid^2) / (n() - n_distinct(paste(pop_year_event, life_stage_simple)))),
            .groups = "drop")

load_events = events %>%
  filter(n_ad >= min_swabs_unit, n_sub >= min_swabs_unit,
         pos_ad >= min_pos_screen, pos_sub >= min_pos_screen) %>%
  left_join(sd_log_load, by = "taxon_capture") %>%
  mutate(contrast = mean_ll_sub - mean_ll_ad,
         se = sd_ll * sqrt(1 / pos_sub + 1 / pos_ad))

# events per species: what each part rests on
full_join(count(prev_events, taxon_capture, name = "prevalence_events"),
          count(load_events, taxon_capture, name = "load_events"), by = "taxon_capture") %>%
  arrange(desc(prevalence_events))

# how much weather varies among the co-sampled events (sd of each part, per species): a slope
# needs spread. within-season spread is near 0 where co-sampled events are one per site-year
prev_events %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), across(c(temp_within, precip_within, temp_year, precip_year),
                            ~ round(sd(.x), 2)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(n))

# site climate among the populations with co-sampled events, per species: the between-site slopes
# rest on species with several such populations spanning a climate range
prev_events %>%
  distinct(taxon_capture, population, site_temp, site_temp_seas, site_precip, site_precip_seas) %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture) %>%
  summarise(n_populations = n(),
            across(c(site_temp, site_temp_seas, site_precip, site_precip_seas),
                   ~ round(max(.x) - min(.x), 2), .names = "{.col}_range"),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_populations))

```

# Models
```{r}
# one meta-regression per part, with each event's sampling se known:
#   contrast | se(se, sigma = TRUE)   y ~ N(mu, sqrt(sigma^2 + se^2)); sigma = event-to-event
#                                     variation beyond sampling noise
#   1 + temp_within + precip_within + temp_year + precip_year
#                                     mean contrast and its slopes (per degree C, per doubling of
#                                     10-day precipitation)
#   (1 + temp_within + precip_within | taxon_capture)
#                                     species mean contrasts and within-season slopes vary by
#                                     species (the population-level slope is then roughly a
#                                     species-weighted average). between-year slopes are shared,
#                                     to keep parameters few for sparse species
#   (1 | taxon_capture:population)    site-level contrasts
# no site-year level: co-sampled events are nearly one per site-year (e.g. r. sierrae 182 events,
# 161 site-years), so a site-year sd and sigma would not be separable (as R2 in stage 1).
# the null model drops the environment terms; comparing sigma and the site sd between the two
# says how much of the contrast's variation the environment explains.
env_formula = bf(contrast | se(se, sigma = TRUE) ~ 1 + temp_within + precip_within + temp_year +
                   precip_year + (1 + temp_within + precip_within | taxon_capture) +
                   (1 | taxon_capture:population))
null_formula = bf(contrast | se(se, sigma = TRUE) ~ 1 + (1 | taxon_capture) +
                    (1 | taxon_capture:population))
# site model: the environment model plus long-term site climate (shared slopes, to keep
# parameters few). comparing the site sd with the environment model says how much of the
# between-site variation in the contrast site climate explains (Q8)
site_formula = bf(contrast | se(se, sigma = TRUE) ~ 1 + temp_within + precip_within + temp_year +
                    precip_year + site_temp + site_temp_seas + site_precip + site_precip_seas +
                    (1 + temp_within + precip_within | taxon_capture) +
                    (1 | taxon_capture:population))

# priors: weakly informative on the contrast scale (logit for prevalence, log load for load).
# slopes normal(0, 0.5): a 1 degree C or one doubling change moving the contrast by more than
# ~1 unit is implausible. sds as in stage 1: intercepts exponential(1), slopes exponential(2)
screen_priors = function(env = TRUE, intercept_sd = 2) {
  p = set_prior(paste0("normal(0, ", intercept_sd, ")"), class = "Intercept") +
    set_prior("exponential(1)", class = "sd") +
    set_prior("exponential(1)", class = "sigma")
  if (env) {
    p = p + set_prior("normal(0, 0.5)", class = "b") +
      set_prior("exponential(2)", class = "sd", group = "taxon_capture", coef = "temp_within") +
      set_prior("exponential(2)", class = "sd", group = "taxon_capture", coef = "precip_within") +
      set_prior("lkj(2)", class = "cor")
  }
  p
}

fit_screen = function(formula, data, prior, name) {
  brm(formula, data = data, family = gaussian(), prior = prior,
      control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 12),
      chains = 4, iter = 4000, warmup = 2000, seed = 128, cores = 4, backend = "cmdstanr",
      file = file.path(screen_dir, name), file_refit = "on_change")
}

screen_fits = list(
  prevalence_env  = fit_screen(env_formula,  prev_events, screen_priors(TRUE, 2),  "screen_prevalence_env"),
  prevalence_null = fit_screen(null_formula, prev_events, screen_priors(FALSE, 2), "screen_prevalence_null"),
  load_env        = fit_screen(env_formula,  load_events, screen_priors(TRUE, 3),  "screen_load_env"),
  load_null       = fit_screen(null_formula, load_events, screen_priors(FALSE, 3), "screen_load_null"),
  prevalence_site = fit_screen(site_formula, prev_events, screen_priors(TRUE, 2),  "screen_prevalence_site"),
  load_site       = fit_screen(site_formula, load_events, screen_priors(TRUE, 3),  "screen_load_site"))

# same-condition species contrasts for the predictive model's sensitivity fit (README "Downstream
# models"): the null model with species as FIXED effects, so each species' contrast rests on its
# own co-sampled events. the random-effect null above pulls species toward the cross-species
# mean; feeding those into a cross-species model would pool twice (trait slopes and between-
# species variance too small). weakly informative prior on each species' contrast
species_formula = bf(contrast | se(se, sigma = TRUE) ~ 0 + taxon_capture +
                       (1 | taxon_capture:population))
species_priors = function(contrast_sd) {
  set_prior(paste0("normal(0, ", contrast_sd, ")"), class = "b") +
    set_prior("exponential(1)", class = "sd") +
    set_prior("exponential(1)", class = "sigma")
}
screen_fits$prevalence_species = fit_screen(species_formula, prev_events, species_priors(2),
                                            "screen_prevalence_species")
screen_fits$load_species = fit_screen(species_formula, load_events, species_priors(3),
                                      "screen_load_species")

# sampler checks (thresholds in conv_check)
map_dfr(screen_fits, conv_check, .id = "fit")

```

# Results
```{r}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 10

# population-level slopes: change in the contrast per degree C (temperature) or per doubling of
# 10-day precipitation. median, 50 / 95% intervals, pd
# env = weather terms only; site = weather + long-term site climate (site_* terms; the weather
# slopes should barely move between the two)
slope_draws = imap_dfr(screen_fits[c("prevalence_env", "load_env", "prevalence_site", "load_site")],
                       function(fit, name) {
  as_draws_df(fit, variable = "^b_(temp|precip|site)_", regex = TRUE) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    pivot_longer(starts_with("b_"), names_to = "term", values_to = "value") %>%
    mutate(part = sub("_(env|site)$", "", name), model = sub("^.*_", "", name),
           term = sub("^b_", "", term))
})

(slope_summary = slope_draws %>%
  group_by(part, model, term) %>%
  summarise(median = median(value),
            lower_50 = quantile(value, 0.25), upper_50 = quantile(value, 0.75),
            lower_95 = quantile(value, 0.025), upper_95 = quantile(value, 0.975),
            pd = max(mean(value > 0), mean(value < 0)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3))))

ggplot(slope_draws %>% filter(model == "site"), aes(x = value, y = term)) +
  stat_halfeye(.width = c(0.5, 0.95), normalize = "panels") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ part, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "change in the subadult - adult contrast per step (see the events chunk for units)",
       y = NULL,
       subtitle = paste("population-level slopes (site model); *_within = within season,",
                        "*_year = between years at a site, site_* = long-term site climate")) +
  theme_classic()

# how much the environment explains: event-level sd (sigma) and site sd, null vs environment
# model. separate fits, so compare posterior summaries (not paired draws)
(variance_explained = imap_dfr(screen_fits, function(fit, name) {
  posterior_summary(fit, variable = c("sigma", "sd_taxon_capture:population__Intercept"),
                    probs = c(0.025, 0.975)) %>%
    as_tibble(rownames = "parameter") %>%
    mutate(fit = name)
}) %>%
  separate(fit, into = c("part", "model"), sep = "_") %>%
  select(part, model, parameter, Estimate, Q2.5, Q97.5) %>%
  arrange(part, parameter, model))

# out-of-sample comparison per part (small models: loo is cheap here)
map(c(prevalence = "prevalence", load = "load"), function(p) {
  loo_compare(list(null = loo(screen_fits[[paste0(p, "_null")]]),
                   env = loo(screen_fits[[paste0(p, "_env")]]),
                   site = loo(screen_fits[[paste0(p, "_site")]])))
})

```

## Species slopes (within season)
```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 10

# species-level within-season slopes (population slope + species deviation), for species with
# >= 10 co-sampled events in that part (fewer: the slope is mostly the population mean)
species_slopes = imap_dfr(list(prevalence = prev_events, load = load_events), function(ev, part) {
  fit = screen_fits[[paste0(part, "_env")]]
  keep = ev %>% count(taxon_capture) %>% filter(n >= 10) %>% pull(taxon_capture)
  fit %>%
    spread_draws(b_temp_within, b_precip_within,
                 r_taxon_capture[taxon_capture, term]) %>%
    filter(term %in% c("temp_within", "precip_within"), taxon_capture %in% keep) %>%
    mutate(value = if_else(term == "temp_within", b_temp_within, b_precip_within) + r_taxon_capture,
           part = part) %>%
    group_by(part, taxon_capture, term) %>%
    median_qi(value, .width = c(0.5, 0.95))
})

ggplot(species_slopes %>% filter(.width == 0.95),
       aes(x = value, xmin = .lower, xmax = .upper, y = taxon_capture)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_pointrange(size = 0.3) +
  facet_grid(part ~ term, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "within-season slope (median, 95%)", y = NULL,
       subtitle = "species with >= 10 co-sampled events in that part") +
  theme_classic()

```

# Same-condition species contrasts
```{r}
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-width: 10

# per species: the contrast at its average co-sampled event (fixed-species null model), as
# posterior mean and sd for the predictive model's sensitivity fit. same scales as stage 1:
# prevalence = logit difference (positive = subadults more often infected), load = difference in
# mean log load among positives. note: the Haldane correction (+0.5 per cell) pulls extreme
# prevalence contrasts slightly toward 0; not corrected
species_draws_sc = imap_dfr(list(prevalence = prev_events, load = load_events), function(ev, part) {
  as_draws_df(screen_fits[[paste0(part, "_species")]], variable = "^b_taxon_capture", regex = TRUE) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    select(starts_with("b_")) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "taxon_capture", values_to = "contrast") %>%
    mutate(taxon_capture = sub("^b_taxon_capture", "", taxon_capture), part = part)
})

same_condition_contrasts = species_draws_sc %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, part) %>%
  summarise(contrast_mean = mean(contrast), contrast_sd = sd(contrast),
            contrast_skew = mean(((contrast - mean(contrast)) / sd(contrast))^3),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(bind_rows(prevalence = count(prev_events, taxon_capture, name = "n_events"),
                      load = count(load_events, taxon_capture, name = "n_events"), .id = "part"),
            by = c("taxon_capture", "part"))

same_condition_contrasts %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  arrange(part, desc(n_events))

# half-eye check: roughly symmetric, unimodal shapes support mean and sd as the summary
species_draws_sc %>%
  mutate(part = factor(part, levels = c("prevalence", "load"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = contrast, y = taxon_capture)) +
  stat_halfeye(.width = c(0.5, 0.95), normalize = "groups", point_size = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey60") +
  facet_wrap(~ part, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "same-condition contrast (median, 50 / 95% intervals)", y = NULL,
       subtitle = "species contrasts from co-sampled events only (fixed-species null model)") +
  theme_classic()

```

# Mantel-Haenszel check (prevalence)
```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 11

# why (2026-11-26): the same-condition prevalence contrasts came out much smaller than the stage 1
# ones, most of all in the balanced, data-rich rana (r. sierrae 0.99 -> 0.39), where timing cannot
# explain it. suspected cause: compression. a co-sampled event has as few as 5 swabs per stage, and
# at 0/5 or 5/5 the Haldane-corrected logit tops out near +/- 2.4, truncating event-level
# differences wherever prevalence is near 0% or 100%.
# check: the Mantel-Haenszel pooled log odds ratio per species across its co-sampled events, the
# classic estimator for many small stratified 2 x 2 tables. it pools the tables' cross-products
# before taking the log, so sparse and all-or-nothing cells do not hit a ceiling. variance:
# Robins-Breslow-Greenland. it assumes one common odds ratio across events (between-event
# variation not modeled), so its se is a lower bound when the contrast varies between events.
# reading: MH close to stage 1 -> compression confirmed (the empirical prevalence response is the
# problem, not the stage 1 contrasts); MH close to the empirical values -> the gap is real
# (same-condition vs realized)
#
# cells per event (subadult = exposed group, so log OR = subadult - adult on the logit scale):
#   a = subadult positive, b = subadult negative, c = adult positive, d = adult negative
mh_prevalence = prev_events %>%
  transmute(taxon_capture,
            a = pos_sub, b = n_sub - pos_sub, c = pos_ad, d = n_ad - pos_ad,
            n = n_sub + n_ad) %>%
  mutate(R = a * d / n, S = b * c / n, P = (a + d) / n, Q = (b + c) / n) %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture) %>%
  summarise(n_events = n(),
            sum_R = sum(R), sum_S = sum(S),
            # RBG variance terms
            v1 = sum(P * R), v2 = sum(P * S + Q * R), v3 = sum(Q * S),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(mh_log_or = if_else(sum_R > 0 & sum_S > 0, log(sum_R / sum_S), NA_real_),
         mh_se = sqrt(v1 / (2 * sum_R^2) + v2 / (2 * sum_R * sum_S) + v3 / (2 * sum_S^2)),
         mh_se = if_else(is.na(mh_log_or), NA_real_, mh_se)) %>%
  select(taxon_capture, n_events, mh_log_or, mh_se)

# species where MH is not defined (no event with the informative cross-product): listed, not used
mh_prevalence %>% filter(is.na(mh_log_or))

# side by side: stage 1 mean contrast (03), empirical same-condition contrast (fixed-species null
# model above), Mantel-Haenszel
stage1_prevalence = read_csv(file.path(intermediates_dir, "03_predictive_responses.csv"),
                             show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(part == "prevalence") %>%
  select(taxon_capture, tier, stage1_mean = contrast_mean, stage1_sd = contrast_sd)

mh_compare = mh_prevalence %>%
  left_join(same_condition_contrasts %>% filter(part == "prevalence") %>%
              select(taxon_capture, empirical_mean = contrast_mean, empirical_sd = contrast_sd),
            by = "taxon_capture") %>%
  left_join(stage1_prevalence, by = "taxon_capture")

mh_compare %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_events))

# how far each same-condition estimate sits from stage 1, over the species with all three
# (slope of each on stage 1 through the origin: 1 = same scale, < 1 = compressed)
mh_compare %>%
  filter(!is.na(mh_log_or), !is.na(stage1_mean)) %>%
  summarise(n_species = n(),
            slope_mh_on_stage1 = round(sum(mh_log_or * stage1_mean) / sum(stage1_mean^2), 2),
            slope_empirical_on_stage1 = round(sum(empirical_mean * stage1_mean) / sum(stage1_mean^2), 2),
            median_abs_diff_mh = round(median(abs(mh_log_or - stage1_mean)), 2),
            median_abs_diff_empirical = round(median(abs(empirical_mean - stage1_mean)), 2))

mh_compare %>%
  filter(!is.na(mh_log_or)) %>%
  select(taxon_capture, stage1_mean, stage1_sd, mh = mh_log_or, mh_se, empirical = empirical_mean,
         empirical_sd) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(mh, empirical), names_to = "estimator", values_to = "estimate") %>%
  mutate(se = if_else(estimator == "mh", mh_se, empirical_sd)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = stage1_mean, y = estimate, color = estimator)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey85") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey85") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = estimate - 1.96 * se, ymax = estimate + 1.96 * se), width = 0, alpha = 0.35) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(x = "stage 1 prevalence contrast (logit)", y = "same-condition estimate (logit)",
       color = NULL, subtitle = "co-sampled events only; 95% bars; dashed = 1:1") +
  theme_classic()

```

# Binomial same-condition prevalence contrasts
```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 11

# why (2026-11-27): the Mantel-Haenszel check recovered only part of the gap between the
# empirical same-condition prevalence contrasts and stage 1 (r. sierrae 0.39 -> 0.61 vs 0.99;
# r. muscosa unchanged at ~0.45 vs 1.29). two estimators, two different limits: the empirical
# logits hit a ceiling in small all-or-nothing cells (Haldane), Mantel-Haenszel assumes one common
# odds ratio across events. a binomial model on the co-sampled events has neither limit: counts
# per event and stage (no ceiling), and the contrast may vary between events, as in stage 1.
#
#   positives | trials(swabs)                 Bd-positive swabs (co100) of that stage in that event
#   0 + taxon_capture + taxon_capture:stage_c each species' midpoint and its contrast as fixed
#                                             effects (no pooling across species, as the
#                                             fixed-species null model above)
#   (1 + stage_c | taxon_capture:pop_year_event)
#                                             event-level intercepts and contrasts; one event-level
#                                             contrast sd shared across species (a simplification:
#                                             most species have few co-sampled events)
#   (1 | taxon_capture:population)            site-level intercepts
# stage_c = -0.5 adult / +0.5 subadult, so the taxon_capture:stage_c coefficient is the species'
# subadult - adult difference in logit prevalence at a typical co-sampled event (stage 1's scale
# and sign). priors as stage 1: coefficients normal(0, 2), intercept sds exponential(1), the
# contrast sd exponential(2), correlation lkj(2)
binomial_events = contrast_data %>%
  semi_join(prev_events, by = c("taxon_capture", "pop_year_event")) %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, population, pop_year_event, stage_c) %>%
  summarise(swabs = n(), positives = sum(.data[[response_col]] > 0), .groups = "drop")

binomial_events %>% summarise(rows = n(), events = n_distinct(paste(taxon_capture, pop_year_event)),
                              species = n_distinct(taxon_capture))

binomial_priors = set_prior("normal(0, 2)", class = "b") +
  set_prior("exponential(1)", class = "sd") +
  set_prior("exponential(2)", class = "sd", group = "taxon_capture:pop_year_event", coef = "stage_c") +
  set_prior("lkj(2)", class = "cor")

fit_binomial = brm(positives | trials(swabs) ~ 0 + taxon_capture + taxon_capture:stage_c +
                     (1 + stage_c | taxon_capture:pop_year_event) + (1 | taxon_capture:population),
                   data = binomial_events, family = binomial(), prior = binomial_priors,
                   control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 12),
                   chains = 4, iter = 4000, warmup = 2000, seed = 128, cores = 4, backend = "cmdstanr",
                   file = file.path(screen_dir, "screen_prevalence_binomial"), file_refit = "on_change")

conv_check(fit_binomial)

# species contrasts: posterior mean, sd and skewness of each taxon_capture:stage_c coefficient
binomial_draws = as_draws_df(fit_binomial, variable = ":stage_c$", regex = TRUE) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(starts_with("b_")) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "contrast") %>%
  mutate(taxon_capture = sub("^b_taxon_capture(.*):stage_c$", "\\1", parameter))

binomial_contrasts = binomial_draws %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture) %>%
  summarise(contrast_mean = mean(contrast), contrast_sd = sd(contrast),
            contrast_skew = mean(((contrast - mean(contrast)) / sd(contrast))^3), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(count(prev_events, taxon_capture, name = "n_events"), by = "taxon_capture")

# all four side by side: stage 1, binomial, Mantel-Haenszel, empirical. reading:
#   binomial close to stage 1           -> the earlier gap was the estimators (ceiling, common OR)
#   binomial close to MH / empirical    -> the within-event contrast really is smaller than stage 1
#                                          (stage 1 carries a realized component in that species)
#   binomial between MH and stage 1     -> heterogeneity between events matters (common OR too
#                                          simple), the rest is realized
binomial_compare = mh_compare %>%
  left_join(binomial_contrasts %>% select(taxon_capture, binomial_mean = contrast_mean,
                                          binomial_sd = contrast_sd),
            by = "taxon_capture") %>%
  select(taxon_capture, n_events, tier, stage1_mean, binomial_mean, binomial_sd, mh_log_or,
         empirical_mean)

binomial_compare %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_events))

# slopes through the origin on stage 1 (1 = same scale, < 1 = smaller), species with all four
binomial_compare %>%
  filter(!is.na(mh_log_or), !is.na(binomial_mean), !is.na(stage1_mean)) %>%
  summarise(n_species = n(),
            across(c(binomial_mean, mh_log_or, empirical_mean),
                   ~ round(sum(.x * stage1_mean) / sum(stage1_mean^2), 2), .names = "slope_{.col}"))

binomial_draws %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = contrast, y = taxon_capture)) +
  stat_halfeye(.width = c(0.5, 0.95), normalize = "groups", point_size = 1) +
  geom_point(data = binomial_compare %>% filter(!is.na(stage1_mean)),
             aes(x = stage1_mean, y = taxon_capture), inherit.aes = FALSE,
             shape = 4, color = "firebrick", size = 2.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey60") +
  labs(x = "same-condition prevalence contrast, binomial model (median, 50 / 95%)", y = NULL,
       subtitle = "red x = stage 1 mean contrast") +
  theme_classic()

```
